scope: IDE native symbol rename action, XUI preview/consent/nonmodal application/manual recovery, asynchronous main-window quit coordination and scaled scrollable file review

materialDependencies.purpose: Exact unchanged native service,118 objects,72 core archive members and prior85 protocol cases; not rebuilt/rerun this stage
Exact prior137-unit GUI and matched SDK used to reproduce the3 additional legacy fixture failures

evidenceNotes: Add editor.renameSymbol action98 and Ctrl+F2 to the Edit menu; file.rename keeps F2. A lazily created XUI window captures source document identity/revision/caret, obtains actual negotiated native RPC candidates, admits the complete managed host protection policy and presents all affected files, edit counts and editor-versus-disk effects before exact-token consent. The API remains limited to verified native candidates; standard rename/applyEdit are not enabled.

Preview/name/confirmation stays modal. The application window reopens without a backdrop, preserves editor focus and allows typing/undo/IME while source operations and new builds are disabled by action policy and existing underlying document/source barriers. Large body/candidate assets stay in existing worker-owned leases. UI review is bounded to512 rows and1MiB known label text, with no silent truncation or partial approval on allocation/SDK-list failure.

Main-window close first requests asynchronous cancellation. Only after physical completion, closed source resources and reader release does it replay the ordinary quit callback once, using existing unsaved-state decisions. A held source write and direct Save/Close rejection are exercised; ordinary quit never reaches workspace save/discard before that barrier ends.

Uncertainty exposes an explicit manual recovery window without releasing holds or replaying frozen logs. It retains/copies the dedicated recovery path, offers directory opening and editor return, and requires a fresh explicit discard confirmation before exiting. That confirmation binds the native token and current document revision/model metadata; later edits invalidate prior approval. Recovery data is not claimed to contain every unsaved body. Automatic verification/resumption remains open.

Business dialogs still default to modal. SetModal only accepts a closed managed window. When preview controls become disabled, focus is explicitly moved to the enabled modal Cancel control so Escape stays within the window. Nonmodal progress/results do not steal editor focus. Creation failure destroys attached/orphaned controls and leaves no false-ready view, allowing retry.

Large-font screenshot review found that the initial footer-only geometry assertion missed a zero-height file list. The final body uses natural-height scrolling with fixed action footer, and file-row metrics scale at lazy creation through existing UI font metrics. The final40DIP case asserts list height, scaled row height, actual visible intersection after scrolling and footer bounds; normal preview, held progress, recovery and large-font screenshots plus two actual C/xlang GUI renders were inspected.

Final29 IDE cases include the original15 internal managed/barrier cases and14 public UI cases: real Ctrl+F2/menu identity, normal five-file commit and C/xlang input, C input while an actual positive source write is held, main-window close deferral and one ordinary replay, preview-generation close button, confirmation Escape, frozen committed journal with repeated/invalidated exit consent, tree-construction failure/retry, stale preview cancellation, no-workspace single-file rename, complete-list failure cancellation, rejected invalid name, two successive public renames on the same worker with distinct scopes/tokens,40DIP review and an actual Cancel click during held writing.

Fresh747-check NativeWork,9-mode async driver,7 original controller/barrier integration groups and55 matched GUI suites pass against final137 rebuilt GUI units and the same native service. Counts are observed assertions, not distinct-feature or performance quantities. Source ReadFull/CondWait counters cover named project imports only; existing full Current/path/configuration preparation and cold UI/OS/SDK work remain outside any zero-I/O or latency claim.

Nine actual compiled bad implementations fail assertions: modal progress, abandoned modal focus, quit before drain, skipped uncertainty consent, stale discard approval, accepted incomplete preview, reenabled source actions, hidden large-font file list and unscaled rows. Every changed include is proven selected by its actual compile dependency closure; compile errors/crashes are not counted as rejected implementations.

Three extra legacy fixtures fail on the final candidate and on the exact prior GUI baseline. dialog_layout_test reports the references-window footer outside its client at40DIP; dialog_message_test fails its first new-project window assertion; modal_open_latency_test refuses its second About opening. Raw failed statuses/logs/programs are retained, their matching assertions are recorded and none is counted as a passing test or timing qualification.

Early quick fixture compilation used a nonexistent SDK getter and was corrected. A held-uncertainty fixture initially attempted disk reads before teardown; the original exclusive handles correctly refused them, so the oracle was moved after app destruction without weakening production policy. A real Escape focus bug and actual large-font list disappearance were then fixed and the complete final UI cases rerun. A later scaled-row compile lacked its explicit header and failed; final source has the declaration and all137 units rebuilt. Intermediate snapshots and failed logs remain immutable.

Two independent helper runs initially collided on reused private DLL aliases and rejected before overwrite. Final helpers use independent names or sequential ownership; exact hash cleanup and final inventory pass. A read-only identity collector was explicitly stopped after detecting an invalid generated row filter before final evidence publication; its corrected replacement completed all actual dependency/hash checks. These failed/helper attempts are not counted as successful acceptance.

The unchanged accepted4c53 native service was not rebuilt. Its118 objects,72 raw core members, actual source/header closure and four unchanged protocol tools are reverified. Prior85 protocol cases are explicitly referenced through their committed index, not presented as fresh runs. All executables execute through root release/win_x64 matched private aliases to protect the user working cohort.

Canonical production source/header parity, compiler inputs, private service-basename-only units, actual test/mutant/baseline link inputs and runtime/SDK identities are bound. The normal runtime, matched developer SDK, active delivery and existing user temporary directories are unchanged. Large source/evidence bundles stay external and indexed; concurrent unrelated staged/worktree state is preserved.
limits: Native IDE rename UI is enabled in the qualified candidate only; standard textDocument/rename, generic workspace/applyEdit and arbitrary-client write activation remain open. This window provides manual uncertain recovery/discard exit, not automatic journal replay or verified in-session resumption.
The3 additional legacy dialog failures remain unresolved, including references layout at40DIP. The55 passing matched suites and29 IDE cases do not establish that every IDE feature/test is green.

Existing ordinary local fixed-drive/single-link/ancestor pin rules and source budgets remain. The6-reader graph does not represent every possible independent reader or an OS-wide transaction. No implicit resume of lost/uncertain state is allowed.
UI metadata/body budgets are not total RSS bounds. Complete Current retains existing path/configuration costs. Whole-goal cold/incremental latency, memory and endurance qualification remains open.

Engine/native asset alignment, complete generic/unbound/foreign qualification, other synchronous readers, deep unprefixed xlp handling, configuration-cache count regression, Linux and sanitizer validation remain open.
C LSP stays disabled. No DAP/runtime/debug completion. Working runtime, developer SDK and active delivery are not replaced or published.
